case_title: State of Punjab v. Kewal Krishan
confession: Extra-judicial confession, but not relied on
neutral_facts: The deceased was last seen alive in his own house in the company of the accused at about 7.00 p.m. on 10.12.1998. The dead body of the deceased with multiple injuries was found in his house by his nephew on 12.12.1998 at around 1.00 p.m. An autopsy conducted on 12.12.1998 indicated that death could have occurred within two days due to shock and haemorrhage from ante mortem incised wounds. The accused made an extra-judicial confession before PW-3 on 25.12.1998 and disclosed the location of a knife used in the crime, which was recovered. The prosecution argued that the knife caused the incised wounds found on the deceased's body. The trial court convicted the accused based on these circumstances, but the High Court acquitted him, finding the evidence insufficient to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
